source_text:
Παρακαλῶ οὖν πάντας ὑμᾶς, πειθαρχεῖν τῷ λόγῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἀσκεῖν πᾶσαν ὑπομονήν, ἣν καὶ εἴδατε κατ’ ὀφθαλμοὺς οὐ μόνον ἐν τοῖς μακαρίοις Ἰγνατίῳ καὶ Ζωσίμῳ καὶ Ῥούφῳ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις τοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἀποστόλοις:
πεπεισμένους ὅτι οὗτοι πάντες οὐκ εἰς κενὸν ἔδραμον, ἀλλ’ ἐν πίστει καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ, καὶ ὅτι εἰς τὸν ὀφειλόμενον αὐτοῖς τόπον εἰσὶ παρὰ τῷ κυρίῳ, ᾧ καὶ συνέπαθον. οὐ γὰρ τὸν νῦν ἠγάπησαν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀποθανόντα καὶ δἰ ἡμᾶς ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναστάντα.
thought_title: Imitate the endurance you saw in the martyrs and apostles
orientation: Polycarp is urging the Philippians to obey the word of righteousness and to practice endurance, pointing to the examples of Ignatius, Zosimus, Rufus, Paul, and the other apostles.
pass_a_gloss: I urge therefore all [of] you, to obey the word of the righteousness and to practice all endurance, which also you saw with [your] eyes not only in the blessed Ignatius and Zosimus and Rufus, but also in others the [ones] from among you and in Paul himself and the remaining apostles: [you] being persuaded that these all not into emptiness ran, but in faith and righteousness, and that into the owed to them place they are with the Lord, with whom also they suffered together. For not the present they loved age, but the [one] for us having died and because of us by God having been raised.

choices.why: Keeps the genitive construction literal and matches the glossary rendering of δικαιοσύνη as righteousness.
πᾶσαν with an abstract noun suggests every form or kind; 'practice' captures ἀσκεῖν's sense of disciplined exercise.
Idiomatic rendering of the phrase meaning 'before your eyes' or 'with your eyes'; 'own' makes the second person explicit.
Echoes Pauline athletic imagery (Gal 2:2; Phil 2:16); 'in vain' is the standard rendering of εἰς κενόν.

choices.english: in the place owed to them
choices.why: Preserves the passive participle ὀφειλόμενον and the dative of advantage; 'owed' keeps the sense of a due reward.
rejected: in the place due to them

choices.english: the one who died for us
choices.why: ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν with the aorist participle of ἀποθνῄσκω is standardly 'died for us'; keeps the articular participle as a substantive.
rejected: him who died on our behalf
the one having died for us

bible_refs.note: οὐκ εἰς κενὸν ἔδραμον echoes Paul's language of running not in vain.
εἰς κενὸν ἔδραμον recalls Paul's phrase about not running in vain.

pass_b_english: So I urge all of you: obey the word of righteousness and practice every kind of endurance. You saw this endurance with your own eyes, not only in the blessed Ignatius, Zosimus, and Rufus, but also in others from among you, and in Paul himself and the rest of the apostles.

Be persuaded that none of these ran in vain. They ran in faith and righteousness, and they are now in the place owed to them, beside the Lord with whom they also suffered. For they did not love this present age. They loved the one who died for us and was raised by God for our sake.

polish.changed: I split the long sentence into shorter ones, clarified that 'these' refers to the martyrs and apostles, and made the final contrast between loving the present age and loving Christ explicit.

problems.quote: they are now in the place owed to them
problems.why: 'Place owed to them' is an odd rendering; the Greek likely means 'the place prepared for them' or 'their rightful place.'
problems.fix: Render as 'the place prepared for them' or 'their appointed place.'

edits.old: they are now in the place owed to them
edits.new: they are now in the place prepared for them

fixed: Changed 'place owed to them' to 'place prepared for them' to better render the Greek 'εἰς τὸν ὀφειλόμενον αὐτοῖς τόπον' as their appointed/prepared place.
